map.summary: This document is a comprehensive datasheet for the STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx microcontrollers (STM32F20x). It describes the Cortex-M3 core, memory map and boot options, ART accelerator, bus matrix, DMA, clocks, interrupts, power domains, reset behavior and low-power modes. It catalogs device-dependent peripherals, including timers, GPIO, ADC/DAC, I²C, USART/UART, SPI/I²S, SDIO, USB OTG, CAN, Ethernet, camera interface, RNG, debug and FSMC external-memory support. Package pinouts, signal types, alternate-function mappings and memory-interface configurations are documented alongside electrical operating limits, supply and decoupling guidance, current consumption, oscillator and PLL data, peripheral timing, analog performance, EMC/ESD and flash endurance. Package dimensions, thermal data, ordering codes, comparison tables and revision history are also included, with specifications qualified by stated test conditions and device variants.
map.short_description: STM32F20x architecture, peripherals, pinouts, electrical limits, timing, and package specifications.

sections.title: STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx Overview
sections.summary: Introduces the STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx microcontrollers and summarizes their Cortex-M3 core, memory, I/O, timers, analog peripherals, communication interfaces, connectivity, and debug features. It also identifies available package options and lists the device variants covered by the datasheet.
sections.short_description: Product overview, key features, package options, and supported device variants.

sections.title: Contents: Functional Overview and Electrical Characteristics
sections.summary: Lists the datasheet’s introductory chapters and functional overview, including the core, memory, buses, DMA, clocks, power, low-power modes, timers, and communication peripherals. The contents continue through analog and debug features, pinouts, memory mapping, and the opening topics of the electrical characteristics chapter.
sections.short_description: Contents listing for device architecture, peripherals, pinouts, and specifications.

sections.title: Contents: Electrical Specifications and Packages
sections.summary: Continues the contents with electrical limits and operating conditions, supply currents, wake-up timing, clocks, memory, I/O, timers, communication interfaces, ADC, DAC, temperature sensing, and other peripheral characteristics. It then lists package information, thermal characteristics, ordering information, and revision history.
sections.short_description: Contents listing for electrical limits, peripheral specifications, packages, and revisions.

sections.title: List of Tables
sections.summary: Indexes datasheet tables on device features, peripherals, timers, USARTs, pins, alternate functions, operating conditions, power modes, wake-up timing, and clock characteristics. It continues with PLL and Flash data, electrical limits, I/O behavior, peripheral timing, ADC/DAC and references, external-memory timing, and package details; entries provide titles and page references, not specifications.
sections.short_description: Indexes tables on device features, electrical limits, peripherals, memory, and packages.

sections.title: List of figures
sections.summary: Lists the datasheet figures and their page references. Topics include device compatibility and architecture, power and startup schemes, pinouts and memory maps, current-consumption plots, clock and PLL waveforms, I/O and peripheral timing, ADC/DAC connections, external-memory controller waveforms, SDIO modes, and package outlines, footprints, and markings.
sections.short_description: Indexes diagrams, timing waveforms, and package drawings.

sections.title: Introduction and beginning of device description
sections.summary: Introduces the STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx microcontroller lines, explains that they are referred to collectively as STM32F20x devices, and directs readers to the reference manual, Flash programming manual, and Cortex-M3 technical reference. The assigned lines then begin Section 2, Description.
sections.short_description: Introduces the STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx datasheet and references.

sections.title: STM32F20x family overview
sections.summary: Introduces the STM32F20x family’s Cortex-M3 core, memory, bus architecture, ART Accelerator, analog and timer resources, and communication interfaces. It outlines operating conditions and package choices for STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx devices, then lists representative application areas and points to the family block diagram.
sections.short_description: Overview of STM32F20x architecture, peripherals, operating range, and applications.

sections.title: STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx feature tables
sections.summary: Tables compare STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx variants by Flash and SRAM capacity, peripheral availability and counts, GPIOs, ADC channels, package, CPU frequency, supply voltage, and temperature range. Accompanying notes clarify FSMC bank limitations, SPI/I2S operating modes, and the WLCSP64+2 low-voltage condition.
sections.short_description: Compares memory, peripherals, packages, and operating specifications by device.

sections.title: Family compatibility and board design
sections.summary: Describes pin-to-pin, software, and feature compatibility between STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx devices, as well as their close—but not drop-in—compatibility with STM32F10xxx devices because of differences in power pins and power schemes. Figures illustrate board-design adaptations for LQFP64, LQFP100, and LQFP144 packages, including resistor and reserved-pin arrangements.
sections.short_description: Explains cross-family compatibility and board changes for selected package designs.

sections.title: STM32F20x block diagram
sections.summary: Presents the STM32F20x block diagram, showing the Cortex-M3 core, MPU/NVIC, ART accelerator, Flash and SRAM, FSMC, bus matrix, DMA, power and clock systems, and backup domain. It also maps GPIO ports and the family’s timers, communication interfaces, ADCs, DACs, Ethernet, camera, USB, and external signal groups.
sections.short_description: Maps core, memory, buses, peripherals, clocks, and external interface signals.

sections.title: Peripheral signals and device availability
sections.summary: This continuation of a pin and peripheral mapping lists external-memory signals, display and USB signals, power and oscillator pins, and alternate-function connections for timers, serial interfaces, I2S, and I2C. It also notes timer clock limits and that the camera interface and Ethernet are available only on STM32F207xx devices.
sections.short_description: Lists peripheral signal functions, supply pins, and device-specific availability.

sections.title: Cortex-M3 core, ART accelerator, and MPU
sections.summary: The STM32F20x uses an Arm Cortex-M3 32-bit RISC processor designed for efficient embedded performance and compatibility with Arm tools and software. The ART Accelerator improves execution from Flash using instruction prefetch and a branch cache, with performance equivalent to zero-wait-state execution up to 120 MHz. The optional MPU protects memory regions and supports task isolation, particularly in RTOS applications.
sections.short_description: Describes the processor core, Flash acceleration, and memory protection features.

sections.title: Embedded memory, CRC, and bus matrix
sections.summary: STM32F20x devices provide 128 KB to 1 MB of embedded Flash, plus 512 bytes of OTP memory for critical data. A CRC unit calculates integrity-check codes for data and Flash verification. The devices also include up to 128 KB of system SRAM and 4 KB of backup SRAM retained in Standby or VBAT mode. A 32-bit multi-AHB matrix connects processing and DMA masters to memory and peripherals.
sections.short_description: Summarizes Flash, CRC, SRAM, and the multi-AHB interconnect.

sections.title: AHB matrix diagram and DMA controller
sections.summary: The multi-AHB matrix diagram identifies the Cortex-M3, DMA1 and DMA2, Ethernet, USB HS, Flash, SRAM, FSMC, and peripheral connections. Two general-purpose dual-port DMA controllers each provide eight streams for memory and peripheral transfers. Features include circular buffers, double buffering, hardware requests, software triggers, and independently configurable transfer sizes. DMA supports SPI/I2S, I2C, USART/UART, timers, DAC, SDIO, DCMI, and ADC.
sections.short_description: Shows the bus-matrix connections and explains DMA capabilities and supported peripherals.

sections.title: Flexible static memory controller
sections.summary: The FSMC provides four chip-select outputs and supports PC Card/Compact Flash, SRAM, PSRAM, NOR Flash, and NAND Flash. It includes a write FIFO, permits code execution from external memory except NAND Flash and PC Card, and supports external access up to 60 MHz. Its parallel LCD interface can work with common Intel 8080 and Motorola 6800 controllers and adapt to other LCD interfaces.
sections.short_description: Covers FSMC chip-select modes, external-memory operation, and LCD interfacing.

sections.title: Interrupt controllers
sections.summary: The NVIC supports 16 priority levels and up to 81 maskable interrupt channels, in addition to Cortex-M3 interrupt lines. Its features include low-latency handling, early and late-arriving interrupt processing, tail chaining, and automatic processor-state saving and restoration. The EXTI controller has 23 independently configurable edge-detection lines, with selectable rising, falling, or both-edge triggers and masking; up to 140 GPIOs can connect to its 16 external interrupt lines.
sections.short_description: Explains NVIC interrupt handling and configurable external interrupt/event lines.

sections.title: Clocks, startup, and boot modes
sections.summary: At reset, the factory-trimmed 16 MHz internal RC oscillator is selected. Software can choose it or an external 4–26 MHz source; clock failure can trigger an automatic switch to the internal oscillator and an interrupt. Prescalers and PLLs configure AHB and APB domains, and PLLI2S supports standard audio sampling rates from 8 to 192 kHz. Boot pins select user Flash, system memory, or SRAM; the system-memory loader supports reprogramming through listed serial, CAN, and USB DFU interfaces.
sections.short_description: Describes clock sources and limits, failure handling, and startup boot options.

sections.title: Power supplies and supply supervision
sections.summary: VDD supplies I/Os and the internal regulator, while VDDA and VSSA supply analog and related circuitry and must connect to VDD and VSS. VBAT powers the RTC, external clock, 32 kHz oscillator, and backup registers when VDD is absent. Integrated POR/PDR and BOR circuitry holds the device in reset below specified thresholds; option bytes configure BOR levels. A programmable voltage detector can monitor VDD/VDDA and generate an interrupt when voltage crosses its threshold.
sections.short_description: Details supply rails, backup power, reset thresholds, BOR, and voltage monitoring.

sections.title: Voltage regulator operating modes
sections.summary: Covers regulator ON and OFF configurations, including internal-reset behavior and package-dependent activation requirements. In ON mode, software selects main regulation, low-power regulation for Stop, or power-down for Standby; power-down disables kernel circuitry and loses register and SRAM contents. It specifies VCAP capacitors and, for regulator OFF, external 1.2 V supply, PA0 supervisor, and startup voltage and reset requirements.
sections.short_description: Explains regulator modes, VCAP requirements, and external-supply startup conditions.

sections.title: Regulator OFF with internal reset disabled
sections.summary: Explains the WLCSP64+2 regulator OFF/internal reset OFF configuration and its external reset and power-monitoring requirements. Lists integrated reset and voltage-monitoring features that are unavailable in this mode, gives VDD and VCAP startup constraints, and compares regulator/reset configurations across packages.
sections.short_description: Covers reset-disabled operation, required supervision, and package support.

sections.title: Real-time clock and backup domain
sections.summary: Introduces the backup domain, containing the RTC, 4 Kbytes of backup SRAM, and 20 backup registers. Summarizes the RTC calendar, alarms, periodic wakeups, clock sources, calibration, reference-clock detection, and prescaler. Explains backup SRAM and register retention and their supply through VDD or VBAT.
sections.short_description: Summarizes RTC functions, backup storage, clocks, alarms, and retention.

sections.title: Low-power modes and VBAT operation
sections.summary: Outlines the STM32F20x Sleep, Stop, and Standby modes, including which circuitry stops, what state is retained, and available wakeup sources. Also covers VBAT powering the RTC and backup domain, Standby behavior, and the transition into timer-feature material.
sections.short_description: Describes Sleep, Stop, Standby, wakeup sources, and backup-domain power.

sections.title: Timer features and general-purpose timers
sections.summary: Compares advanced-control, general-purpose, and basic timers by counter width, counting modes, prescalers, channels, DMA requests, and clock limits. Describes TIM1/TIM8 PWM and synchronization, TIM2–TIM5 capture, compare, encoder, and Hall-sensor functions, plus TIM9–TIM14, TIM6/TIM7 time bases, watchdogs, and SysTick.
sections.short_description: Compares timer features and covers synchronization, watchdogs, and SysTick.

sections.title: Serial communication and memory-card interfaces
sections.summary: The STM32F20x provides up to three I²C interfaces with multimaster and slave modes, addressing options, CRC, DMA, and SMBus/PMBus support. Six UART/USART interfaces offer asynchronous and additional communication modes, with varying baud rates and feature sets. The section also outlines SPI and I²S capabilities and the SDIO host interface’s card standards, bus widths, transfer rates, and CE-ATA support.
sections.short_description: I²C, USART/UART, SPI, I²S, and SDIO interface features.

sections.title: Ethernet MAC and CAN
sections.summary: Ethernet MAC is available on STM32F207xx devices and supports MII or RMII connection to an external PHY, 10/100 Mbit/s operation, dedicated DMA, frame filtering, buffering, and IEEE 1588 hardware timestamping. The two CAN controllers support standard and extended frames up to 1 Mbit/s, with transmit mailboxes, receive FIFOs, shared filter banks, and dedicated SRAM.
sections.short_description: Ethernet connectivity and the dual CAN controller’s capabilities.

sections.title: USB OTG full-speed and high-speed
sections.summary: The USB OTG full-speed peripheral integrates transceivers and supports device, host, and OTG operation, configurable endpoints, suspend/resume, dynamic FIFO sizing, and SRP/HNP protocols. The high-speed peripheral supports full-speed internally and up to 480 Mbit/s with an external ULPI PHY. Its listed features include larger FIFOs, more endpoints and host channels, internal USB DMA, and power-switch requirements for bus-powered devices.
sections.short_description: USB OTG modes, performance, endpoints, FIFOs, and PHY requirements.

sections.title: Audio PLL, camera interface, and random number generator
sections.summary: The dedicated PLLI2S provides accurate audio sampling clocks from 8 kHz to 192 kHz and can be reconfigured without disabling the main PLL; an external master-clock input can synchronize I²S. The camera interface is available on STM32F207xx and supports parallel capture, multiple pixel formats, continuous or snapshot modes, and automatic cropping. STM32F2xxx products also include a hardware true random number generator.
sections.short_description: Audio clocking, camera capture, and hardware random-number generation.

sections.title: GPIO and ADC
sections.summary: GPIOs support input, push-pull or open-drain output, and alternate-function modes, with optional pulls, speed and current settings, configuration locking, and fast AHB1 access. Three 12-bit ADCs provide up to 16 external channels each, scan and single conversions, simultaneous or interleaved sampling, monitoring, and timer triggers. The two-channel 12-bit DAC supports output modes, triggers, and DMA; the internal temperature sensor is best used to track changes rather than absolute temperature.
sections.short_description: GPIO configuration, ADC conversion and monitoring, DAC capabilities, and temperature sensing.

sections.title: Debug interfaces and embedded trace
sections.summary: Describes the combined JTAG and serial wire debug interface, including the shared TMS/TCK and SWDIO/SWCLK pins and the sequence used to select a debug mode. It also introduces the Embedded Trace Macrocell, which streams compressed instruction and data flow to external trace hardware for recording and debugger display.
sections.short_description: Explains the SWJ-DP debug port and Embedded Trace Macrocell.

sections.title: LQFP64 and WLCSP64+ pinouts
sections.summary: Presents STM32F20x top-view pinout diagrams for the LQFP64 and WLCSP64+ packages. The figures identify package pins and associated signals, including power, reset, oscillator, port, and special-function connections. A note clarifies that the diagrams show the package top view.
sections.short_description: Shows package top-view pin assignments for LQFP64 and WLCSP64+.

sections.title: LQFP100 pinout
sections.summary: Contains the STM32F20x LQFP100 pinout figure, showing package pin numbers alongside signal names. The diagram includes port pins and supply, ground, reference-voltage, reset, oscillator, and capacitor connections. It notes that RFU means reserved for future use and that such a pin may be tied to VDD or VSS, or left unconnected.
sections.short_description: Lists the STM32F20x LQFP100 package pin and signal assignments.

sections.title: LQFP144 pinout
sections.summary: Presents the STM32F20x LQFP144 pinout diagram, mapping package pin numbers to port signals and dedicated connections such as oscillator, reset, supply, ground, and reference pins. The accompanying note defines RFU as reserved for future use and describes the permitted handling of those pins; the figure is a package top view.
sections.short_description: Shows the STM32F20x LQFP144 package’s top-view pin assignments.

sections.title: LQFP176 pinout
sections.summary: Contains the STM32F20x LQFP176 pinout figure, pairing package pin numbers with signal names. The diagram covers GPIO and alternate-function ports, oscillator and reset connections, and power, ground, reference, and capacitor pins. It also identifies package-specific signals such as RTC-related pins and illustrates the physical pin arrangement.
sections.short_description: Shows the STM32F20x LQFP176 package’s top-view pin assignments.

sections.title: UFBGA176 球位图与引脚表图例
sections.summary: 本节展示 STM32F20x UFBGA176 封装的球位图，并说明 RFU 引脚的处理方式及图示为封装顶视图。随后给出引脚表图例，解释引脚名、供电与 I/O 类型、电压容限、I/O 结构、复位状态说明，以及 GPIO 复用功能和外设直接选择功能的区别。
sections.short_description: 介绍 UFBGA176 封装球位图及引脚表所用缩写和标记。

sections.title: 引脚与球位定义：PE、PC、PI、PF 引脚
sections.summary: 引脚与球位定义表列出不同封装（包括 LQFP 与 UFBGA176）的引脚编号、复位后的引脚名、类型、I/O 结构、备注、复用功能及附加功能。本段从 PE2–PE6 等引脚开始，包含 PC13–PC15、PI9–PI11、供电引脚及 PF0–PF5，并列出相应的跟踪、FSMC、I²C、事件输出和 ADC 功能。
sections.short_description: 列出引脚定义表开头的封装编号、引脚类型及功能。

sections.title: 引脚与球位定义：PF、PH、PC 与 PA0
sections.summary: 本段续列 STM32F20x 引脚定义，包括 PF6–PF10、PH0/PH1、PC0–PC3，以及 VDD、VSSA、VREF−、VREF+ 和 VDDA 等电源或参考引脚。表格还给出 PA0-WKUP 的封装编号、I/O 属性及 USART、UART、以太网、定时器、事件输出、ADC 和唤醒功能。
sections.short_description: 继续列出 PF、PH、PC 和 PA0 引脚的封装位置与功能。

sections.title: 引脚与球位定义：PA1–PA7 及 PH2–PH5
sections.summary: 本段继续引脚与球位定义表，覆盖 PA1、PA2、PA3、PA4、PA5、PA6、PA7，以及仅见于较大封装的 PH2–PH5。内容说明各引脚的封装位置、I/O 类型和结构，并列出 USART、SPI、I²S、定时器、以太网、OTG、DCMI、事件输出及 ADC/DAC 等复用或附加功能。
sections.short_description: 列出 PA1–PA7 与 PH2–PH5 的引脚映射和外设功能。

sections.title: 引脚与球位定义：PC4、PC5、PB0–PB2 与 PF11–PF13
sections.summary: 本节续列 STM32F20x 多组引脚的封装引脚号、球位、I/O 类型及复用功能，涉及 PC4–PC5、PB0–PB2/BOOT1、PF11–PF15、PG0–PG1、PE7–PE15、PB10–PB11 和 PH6–PH12。功能包括以太网、定时器、OTG_HS_ULPI、DCMI、FSMC、USART、I2C 等信号，并列出相关 ADC 输入及 EVENTOUT。
sections.short_description: 概述 STM32F20x 多组引脚的封装位置、I/O 类型及复用和附加功能。

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PB12–PB15 and PD8–PD15
sections.summary: Continuation of the STM32F20x pin and ball definitions table. It records package assignments and alternate functions for PB12–PB15 and PD8–PD15, including SPI, I2S, USART, CAN, USB, FSMC, and timer signals, followed by PG2.
sections.short_description: Details package assignments and alternate functions for PB12–PB15 and PD8–PD15.

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PG3–PG8, PC6–PC9, and PA8–PA11
sections.summary: Continuation of Table 8 covering PG3–PG8, PC6–PC9, and PA8–PA11. The entries provide pin locations, I/O characteristics, and alternate functions such as FSMC, USART6, SDIO, DCMI, timers, I2C, CAN, and USB.
sections.short_description: Lists package assignments and peripheral functions for PG, PC, and PA pins.

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PA12–PA15, PH13–PH15, PI0–PI3, and PC10–PC11
sections.summary: Continuation of the STM32F20x pin definitions table, covering PA12–PA15, PH13–PH15, PI0–PI3, and PC10–PC11. Listed alternate functions include CAN, USB, debugging, timers, SPI, I2S, DCMI, UART, and SDIO.
sections.short_description: Describes package assignments and alternate functions for PA, PH, PI, and PC pins.

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PC12, PD0, and PD1
sections.summary: The final lines continue Table 8’s pin and ball definitions, with a repeated and partially disordered header followed by entries for PC12, PD0, and PD1. Their listed functions include I2S, USART, DCMI, SPI, FSMC, CAN, and timer signals.
sections.short_description: Continues the pin-definition table with PC12, PD0, and PD1 functions.

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PD and PG pins
sections.summary: Continues the STM32F20x pin-definition table with PD2–PD7 and PG9–PG12. The entries give package-specific pin locations, pin types and I/O characteristics, and alternate or additional functions, including SDIO, FSMC, USART, DCMI, Ethernet, and event output.
sections.short_description: Lists package positions and alternate functions for PD2–PD7 and PG9–PG12.

sections.title: STM32F20x pin definitions: PG13–PE1 and notes
sections.summary: Continues the pin-definition table with PG13–PG15, PB3–PB9, and PE0–PE1, including their package locations and alternate functions. The accompanying notes explain function availability, reserved pins, FT tolerance, package connections, GPIO output limits, and conditions affecting PA0 in UFBGA176 devices.
sections.short_description: Covers further GPIO pin functions, package details, and explanatory table notes.

sections.title: FSMC pin definitions
sections.summary: Introduces the FSMC pin-definition table for LQFP100, mapping device pins to signals used by CompactFlash, NOR/PSRAM/SRAM, multiplexed memory, and 16-bit NAND configurations. The entries cover address and data lines, control signals, and NAND-specific functions through PD9.
sections.short_description: Maps STM32F20x pins to FSMC signals for memory and CompactFlash interfaces.

sections.title: FSMC pin definitions and alternate-function mapping
sections.summary: Completes FSMC pin assignments for PD, PG, PB, and PE, covering data, address, chip-enable, wait, and byte-lane signals. It then introduces the STM32F20x alternate-function table, listing AF mappings for Port A pins PA0–PA15, including timer, SPI, I2C, USART, CAN, USB, Ethernet, DCMI, debug, and EVENTOUT signals.
sections.short_description: Covers FSMC pin assignments and Port A alternate functions PA0–PA15.

sections.title: Alternate-function mapping: Port B
sections.summary: Introduces the continued alternate-function table and gives mappings for Port B pins PB0–PB15. Listed functions include timer channels, I2C, SPI/I2S, USART, CAN, USB OTG, Ethernet, FSMC, SDIO, and DCMI signals, alongside debug functions and EVENTOUT. Several rows combine mappings for multiple pins.
sections.short_description: Maps Port B pins PB0–PB15 to peripheral and system signals.

sections.title: Alternate-function mapping: Port C
sections.summary: Continues the alternate-function mapping table under the STM32F20xxx heading, covering Port C pins PC0–PC15. The entries include USB OTG and Ethernet signals, timer channels, SPI/I2S, USART and UART, SDIO, and DCMI functions. PC14 and PC15 are identified with oscillator pins; EVENTOUT is shown where applicable.
sections.short_description: Lists Port C alternate functions in the STM32F20xxx table.

sections.title: Alternate-function mapping: Ports D and E
sections.summary: Continues the STM32F20xxx alternate-function table, covering Port D pins PD0–PD15, Port E pins PE0–PE15, and ports F–I. Mappings include CAN, USART, timers, I2C, SDIO, DCMI, Ethernet, trace, FSMC address/data/control signals, and event output.
sections.short_description: Maps alternate peripheral functions for GPIO pins on ports D through I.

sections.title: STM32F20xxx memory mapping
sections.summary: Figure 16 presents the STM32F20xxx memory map across the processor address space, with address ranges for its regions and blocks 5 through 0. The map covers the Cortex-M3 internal peripheral block, peripheral space, FSMC banks, SRAM, bit-banding regions, and code memory; boot-pin settings affect the memory mapping.
sections.short_description: Summarizes Figure 16’s STM32F20xxx address map and its memory regions.

sections.title: Electrical parameter conditions and power supply scheme
sections.summary: The electrical-characteristics notes explain how guaranteed, typical, and characterized values are established, and show pin loading and input-voltage measurement conditions. The supply diagram identifies the device’s power domains, backup circuitry, regulator connections, and recommended capacitors; accompanying cautions emphasize close placement and proper decoupling.
sections.short_description: This section describes electrical test conditions, pin loading, and supply decoupling.

sections.title: Current measurement and absolute maximum ratings
sections.summary: The section shows the current-consumption measurement connections and specifies absolute maximum voltage, current, and thermal ratings. Notes clarify power and ground connection requirements, input-voltage limits, injected-current effects, and the permitted total injection across pins. These limits are stress ratings, not normal operating conditions.
sections.short_description: This section gives current, voltage, and thermal stress limits for the device.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.summary: General operating-condition tables specify internal AHB, APB1, and APB2 clock frequencies, supply ranges for VDD, VDDA, and VBAT, and input-voltage limits for device pins. They also list package-dependent power dissipation and ambient and junction temperature ranges, with notes concerning ADC use, power sequencing, and low-power operation.
sections.short_description: This section lists operating voltage, clock, temperature, and power conditions.

sections.title: Supply-voltage limits and VCAP capacitors
sections.summary: Table 15 relates the operating supply-voltage range to ADC conversion speed, Flash access frequency and wait states, I/O performance, synchronous FSMC clock limits, and permitted Flash erase/program widths. The following figure illustrates wait states versus CPU frequency and supply voltage. The section then specifies the external capacitor for the main regulator’s VCAP1/VCAP2 pins: 2.2 µF with ESR below 2 Ω. When bypassing the regulator, replace the two capacitors with 100 nF decoupling capacitors.
sections.short_description: Operating limits by supply voltage and external capacitor requirements.

sections.title: Power-up, power-down, and reset characteristics
sections.summary: This section gives power-up and power-down timing requirements with the regulator on and off, then lists embedded reset and power-control characteristics. Table 19 provides programmable voltage-detector levels for rising and falling edges, PVD hysteresis, power-on/power-down reset thresholds, brownout thresholds and hysteresis, and reset temporization. The accompanying notes identify design guarantees and measurement conditions. It also introduces the current-consumption data and describes the operating conditions and clock configuration used for those measurements.
sections.short_description: Power sequencing limits and embedded reset and voltage-detector thresholds.

sections.title: Run-mode current consumption
sections.summary: Tables and graphs characterize regulator inrush current and energy at power-on or wakeup, plus typical and maximum Run-mode supply current across HCLK/CPU frequencies and temperatures. Results compare Flash execution with ART enabled or disabled and RAM execution, with peripherals enabled or disabled. Notes cover measurement conditions, SRAM execution, ADC-related consumption, clock conditions, and characterization limits.
sections.short_description: Inrush and Run-mode current across execution modes, clock rates, and conditions.

sections.title: Sleep-mode current consumption
sections.summary: Gives typical and maximum supply current in Sleep mode at several HCLK frequencies, with peripherals enabled or disabled and measurements across temperatures. Includes notes on external-clock conditions and added ADC current, followed by typical current-consumption plots for Sleep mode with peripherals on and off.
sections.short_description: Sleep-mode current tables and typical current-versus-frequency plots.

sections.title: Stop, Standby, and VBAT current consumption
sections.summary: Specifies typical and maximum current in Stop mode for regulator and Flash configurations, with a graph of typical Stop-mode current across temperature. It then lists Standby-mode and VBAT-domain current for backup SRAM, low-speed oscillator, and RTC configurations, including characterization notes.
sections.short_description: Current-consumption specifications for Stop, Standby, and VBAT modes.

sections.title: Peripheral current consumption and wakeup
sections.summary: Explains the measurement conditions for on-chip peripheral current, then tabulates typical consumption for GPIO, bus-connected peripherals, timers, communication interfaces, ADCs, DACs, and power-control blocks. Footnotes define relevant clock and enable settings. The section ends by introducing wakeup-time measurements from low-power modes and the clock source used after Stop or Standby.
sections.short_description: Typical peripheral currents and the start of low-power wakeup timing details.

sections.title: Wakeup timings and external clock characteristics
sections.summary: This section gives the Sleep, Stop, and Standby wakeup timings, followed by specifications for externally generated high-speed and low-speed clock signals. It lists frequency, voltage, timing, capacitance, duty-cycle, and input-leakage limits, and includes AC timing diagrams for both external clock inputs.
sections.short_description: Wakeup timings and electrical characteristics of external clock sources.

sections.title: Crystal and ceramic resonator oscillator characteristics
sections.summary: This section describes using crystal or ceramic resonators for the high-speed external (HSE) and low-speed external (LSE) clocks. It presents oscillator characteristics such as frequency, feedback resistance, current consumption, transconductance, and startup time, and gives component-placement and load-capacitor guidance with typical application diagrams.
sections.short_description: Design guidance and specifications for HSE and LSE crystal oscillators.

sections.title: Internal clock source characteristics
sections.summary: This section specifies the STM32F20xxx internal high-speed (HSI) and low-speed (LSI) RC oscillators. Tables provide their frequencies, trimming or accuracy, startup times, and power consumption, with notes on test conditions and characterization. Temperature-dependent accuracy plots accompany the oscillator data.
sections.short_description: Frequency accuracy, startup, and power data for the HSI and LSI RC oscillators.

sections.title: PLL characteristics
sections.summary: This section specifies the main PLL and PLLI2S (audio PLL) electrical characteristics: input, output, and VCO frequency ranges; lock times across operating frequencies; and cycle-to-cycle jitter for system-clock, MCO, and I2S outputs. It also covers PLL power consumption on VDD and VDDA, Ethernet/CAN-related conditions, and design notes on guarantees and clock-division requirements.
sections.short_description: Main and audio PLL clock ranges, lock times, jitter, power, and operating notes.

sections.title: PLL spread spectrum clock generation
sections.summary: Describes the main PLL’s spread-spectrum clock generation feature for reducing electromagnetic interference. The section specifies modulation frequency and depth limits, provides equations for modulation period and increment step, explains depth quantization, and illustrates center-spread and down-spread output-clock waveforms.
sections.short_description: Spread-spectrum PLL parameters, calculation formulas, and output waveforms.

sections.title: Flash memory characteristics
sections.summary: Presents flash-memory supply current and programming and erase characteristics, including timing by sector size and program/erase parallelism. It also specifies programming-voltage ranges, programming and erase timings with VPP, VPP operating restrictions, endurance, and data-retention figures across stated temperatures and cycling conditions.
sections.short_description: Flash programming, erase timing, VPP use, endurance, and data retention.

sections.title: EMC characteristics
sections.summary: Covers EMC characterization and susceptibility testing, including ESD and fast transient bursts, software measures, and prequalification trials. It describes EMI emission setups and limits, including PLL spread spectrum, then reports human-body and charge-device ESD ratings, latch-up methods, and I/O current-injection susceptibility, with guidance for protecting analog inputs.
sections.short_description: EMC susceptibility and EMI tests, ESD ratings, latch-up, and I/O protection.

sections.title: I/O static characteristics
sections.summary: Lists static I/O characteristics, including low and high input levels, hysteresis, leakage current, and weak pull-up and pull-down resistance. Notes test and design qualifications, then explains CMOS and TTL input compatibility and illustrates how FT I/O thresholds compare with those requirements across supply voltages.
sections.short_description: Input thresholds, leakage, pull resistors, capacitance, and FT I/O behavior.

sections.title: Output drive and voltage levels
sections.summary: Describes GPIO source and sink current capability, restrictions for PC13–PC15 and PI8, and aggregate-current limits tied to the absolute maximum ratings. Gives output low and high voltage characteristics for CMOS and TTL ports at specified currents, with notes on powered-through-switch pins and current limits.
sections.short_description: GPIO drive-current limits and specified output voltage levels.

sections.title: I/O AC characteristics
sections.summary: Presents I/O AC test conditions and output timing specifications, including maximum frequency and rise/fall times across OSPEEDR settings, capacitive loads, and supply voltages. The section also covers NRST input thresholds, pull-up resistance and reset pulse duration, with design notes and a recommended reset protection circuit.
sections.short_description: GPIO output timing specifications and NRST electrical characteristics and protection.

sections.title: TIM Timer Characteristics
sections.summary: Lists characteristics for timers connected to APB1 and APB2, including timer resolution at different clock rates, maximum external clock frequency, counter clock periods, and maximum count durations. It also identifies which timer instances are included in each TIMx grouping.
sections.short_description: Timer resolution, external clock, counter range, and timing across APB domains.

sections.title: I2C Interface Characteristics
sections.summary: Describes STM32F205xx and STM32F207xx I2C pin behavior, including the limitation that SDA and SCL are not true open-drain outputs. The tables specify standard- and fast-mode timing parameters, bus capacitance, and analog-filter spike suppression, with notes on clock requirements and design guarantees.
sections.short_description: I2C protocol notes, standard- and fast-mode timing limits, and table footnotes.

sections.title: I2C Waveforms, SCL Settings, and SPI Characteristics
sections.summary: Presents the I2C measurement circuit and AC waveforms, with SCL frequency and CCR settings for specified clock, voltage, and pull-up conditions. It then details SPI clock limits, duty cycle, rise/fall times, NSS and SCK timing, data setup/hold, output timing, and slave/master timing diagrams.
sections.short_description: I2C waveforms and clock settings, followed by SPI timing limits and diagrams.

sections.title: I2S characteristics and timing diagrams
sections.summary: Presents I2S frequency and timing specifications, including clock rise/fall, WS setup and hold, clock high/low, and data input and output timing for master and slave configurations. Philips-protocol timing diagrams show the CK, WS, and serial-data relationships for both operating modes.
sections.short_description: I2S clock, word-select, and data timing specifications for master and slave.

sections.title: USB OTG FS electrical characteristics
sections.summary: Details USB OTG Full-Speed startup and electrical limits, including operating voltage, receiver input thresholds, output levels, and pull-up/pull-down resistance. The section also specifies data-line rise and fall times, their matching, and crossover voltage, with measurement conditions and notes.
sections.short_description: USB Full-Speed startup, DC levels, driver characteristics, and signal timing.

sections.title: USB HS electrical characteristics and ULPI timing
sections.summary: Specifies USB High-Speed operating-voltage limits and clock timing, including first-transition and steady-state frequency and duty-cycle ranges, settling and startup timing. It also references the ULPI timing diagram and gives control- and data-signal setup, hold, and output timing under stated supply-voltage and temperature conditions.
sections.short_description: USB High-Speed voltage and clock limits, plus ULPI control and data timing.

sections.title: Ethernet and CAN interface characteristics
sections.summary: This section covers Ethernet operating voltage and timing characteristics for the SMI, RMII, and MII interfaces, with diagrams and tables for clock, setup, hold, and signal-valid delays. It also directs readers to the I/O port characteristics for the CAN transmit and receive alternate functions.
sections.short_description: Operating voltage and timing specifications for Ethernet and CAN interfaces.

sections.title: 12-bit ADC characteristics and accuracy
sections.summary: This section specifies 12-bit ADC supply and reference ranges, clock and trigger limits, sampling and conversion times, input impedance, and current consumption. It also describes ADC error measures, injection-current considerations, and the analog input connection model, including how parasitic capacitance can affect conversion accuracy.
sections.short_description: ADC operating limits, conversion timing, accuracy, and input connection guidance.

sections.title: General PCB design guidelines
sections.summary: This section gives PCB guidance for power-supply and reference-voltage decoupling. Figures 54 and 55 show arrangements with VREF+ separate from or connected to VDDA. Use good-quality 10 nF ceramic capacitors placed as close to the device as possible, following the applicable diagram. It also notes which STM32F20xxx packages provide VREF+ and VREF− and how these pins are internally connected when unavailable.
sections.short_description: PCB decoupling guidance, diagrams, and VREF pin availability and connections.

sections.title: DAC electrical characteristics
sections.summary: DAC characteristics include supply and reference ranges, output loading and voltage excursion, quiescent current, linearity, offset and gain errors, settling and update rates, wakeup time, and power-supply rejection. Notes specify test and characterization conditions; a figure describes the 12-bit DAC output buffer and its bypass control.
sections.short_description: Lists DAC operating limits, accuracy, timing, and output-buffer details.

sections.title: Temperature sensor, VBAT monitor, and internal reference
sections.summary: Tables give temperature-sensor voltage, slope, linearity, and startup time; VBAT monitoring bridge, error, and ADC sampling time; and embedded-reference voltage, spread, temperature coefficient, and startup time. Footnotes distinguish characterization-based guarantees from design guarantees and describe sampling-time determination.
sections.short_description: Summarizes electrical characteristics for the sensor and internal references.

sections.title: FSMC asynchronous read characteristics
sections.summary: The asynchronous FSMC section specifies timing configuration assumptions and defines HCLK period notation. A non-multiplexed SRAM/PSRAM/NOR read waveform is followed by timing limits for chip select, output enable, address and byte-lane validity, data setup and hold, and the optional address latch signal, with load and characterization notes.
sections.short_description: Introduces FSMC timing conditions and gives asynchronous read waveforms and limits.

sections.title: FSMC asynchronous write characteristics
sections.summary: Illustrates FSMC asynchronous memory write timing with a non-multiplexed SRAM/PSRAM/NOR waveform, then presents multiplexed PSRAM/NOR read and write waveforms and timing tables. Specifications cover chip select, write enable, address, data, byte lanes, address latch, setup and hold intervals, and signal transitions; the excerpt includes partial tables and measurement notes.
sections.short_description: FSMC asynchronous memory waveforms and read/write timing specifications.

sections.title: Synchronous multiplexed NOR/PSRAM read timings
sections.summary: Introduces synchronous FSMC waveforms and the configuration used for the timing results, including burst access, memory type, write burst, clock division, and data latency settings. Figure 61 and Table 76 describe synchronous multiplexed NOR/PSRAM read timing relationships, including clock, address, control, data, and NWAIT signals.
sections.short_description: Synchronous FSMC waveform configuration and read timing specifications.

sections.title: Synchronous PSRAM write timings and read waveform
sections.summary: Presents FSMC synchronous timing for multiplexed PSRAM writes, including clock-relative signals for chip enable, address, NADV, NWE, data and byte lanes. It then shows the non-multiplexed NOR/PSRAM read waveform and completes FSMC_NWAIT timings for two WAITCFG settings, followed by Table 78’s read-cycle limits for clock, controls and data, with load and characterization notes.
sections.short_description: Write and read timing limits for synchronous FSMC PSRAM and NOR cycles.

sections.title: Synchronous non-multiplexed PSRAM write timing
sections.summary: Shows the synchronous non-multiplexed PSRAM write waveform and Table 79’s clock-relative limits. The listed signals include FSMC_NEx, NADV, address, NWE, data, and NBL. The table continues with additional limits and notes that the values use a 30 pF load and are guaranteed by characterization, not production testing.
sections.short_description: Waveform and timing limits for synchronous non-multiplexed PSRAM writes.

sections.title: PC Card and CompactFlash controller waveforms
sections.summary: Introduces PC Card/CompactFlash synchronous waveforms and gives the FSMC setup values used to obtain the timing results. Figures 65–70 cover common-memory reads and writes, attribute-memory reads and writes, and I/O-space reads and writes. Notes describe inactive chip-select behavior and the data-bus width used for attribute-memory transfers.
sections.short_description: Controller configuration and waveforms for PC Card and CompactFlash accesses.

sections.title: PC Card/CF switching characteristics
sections.summary: Tables 80–83 specify switching characteristics for PC Card/CompactFlash memory and I/O cycles and FSMC NAND Flash read/write cycles. They cover signal timing relative to THCLK, including chip select, register select, output enable, write enable, I/O strobes, data validity, pulse widths, and ALE timing, with measurement and load notes.
sections.short_description: Timing limits for PC Card, CompactFlash, and FSMC NAND read/write cycles.

sections.title: Характеристики DCMI, SDIO и RTC
sections.summary: Представлены частотное соотношение для интерфейса камеры DCMI, диаграммы и характеристики SD/MMC, а также параметры SDIO в режимах высокой и стандартной скорости. В таблице указаны пределы частоты, времена тактового сигнала, настройки и удержания входных и выходных данных. Завершает раздел характеристика частотного отношения для операций RTC.
sections.short_description: Раздел содержит электрические характеристики интерфейсов DCMI, SDIO и RTC.

sections.title: Корпус LQFP64
sections.summary: Описываются сведения о корпусах и экологических классах ECOPACK, затем приведены контур LQFP64 и таблица его механических размеров в миллиметрах и дюймах. Указаны размеры корпуса, выводов и шага, допуски и примечание о пересчёте единиц. Чертёж рекомендуемой посадочной площадки задаёт размеры и расположение контактных площадок.
sections.short_description: Раздел приводит чертежи, механические размеры и рекомендуемую посадочную площадку LQFP64.

sections.title: Маркировка и корпус WLCSP64+2
sections.summary: Раздел описывает правила ориентации маркировки на корпусе и примеры обозначений изделия, даты, ревизии и первого вывода, отмечая возможные различия маркировки в зависимости от поставки. Для корпуса WLCSP64+2 приведены число шариков, габариты и допуски в миллиметрах и дюймах, схема, а также рекомендуемые параметры посадочного места и разводки платы для шага 0,4 мм.
sections.short_description: Раздел охватывает маркировку WLCSP64+2, размеры корпуса и рекомендации по разводке платы.

sections.title: LQFP100 package information and device marking
sections.summary: Describes the 100-pin, 14 × 14 mm LQFP100 package. The section provides its outline drawing, mechanical dimensions and tolerances in millimeters and inches, and recommended PCB footprint. It also shows an example of the package-top marking and pin 1 identifier, with a notice about engineering-sample parts.
sections.short_description: Covers the LQFP100 outline, dimensions, footprint, and marking example.

sections.title: LQFP144 package information and device marking
sections.summary: Covers the 144-pin, 20 × 20 mm LQFP144 package, including its outline and mechanical data table with dimensions and tolerances in millimeters and inches. A recommended footprint drawing follows, then an example of the package-top device marking and pin 1 identifier, alongside the engineering-sample qualification notice.
sections.short_description: Presents LQFP144 mechanical data, footprint guidance, and a marking example.

sections.title: LQFP176 package outline and mechanical data
sections.summary: Covers the LQFP176 (24 × 24 mm) and UFBGA176+25 package outlines and mechanical data, including body and lead or ball-grid dimensions and tolerances in millimeters and inches. It also provides the recommended PCB footprint and design rules for the 0.65 mm-pitch UFBGA package, including pad, soldermask, stencil, and trace specifications.
sections.short_description: Package outlines, mechanical dimensions, and PCB footprint guidance for LQFP176 and UFBGA176+25.

sections.title: Device Marking and Thermal Characteristics
sections.summary: Shows an example of the UFBGA176+25 topside marking and identifies the product, revision and date codes, and ball A1 marker. It cautions that engineering samples are not qualified for production use. The section then gives junction-to-ambient thermal resistance values for several packages and identifies the referenced natural-convection test standard.
sections.short_description: Explains UFBGA device markings and gives package thermal resistance data.

sections.title: Ordering Information
sections.summary: Explains how to interpret an STM32F20xxx order code, using an example to identify the device family, product type, subfamily, pin count, Flash size, package, temperature range, software option, and ordering options. It notes that 66-pin devices are WLCSP-only and directs readers to ST sales for available combinations.
sections.short_description: Decodes STM32F20xxx order codes and describes their selectable device options.

sections.title: Revision History: Revisions 1–4
sections.summary: Lists the first four document revisions, from the initial release in June 2009 through revision 4 in July 2010. Early updates cover the specification status, pin and package corrections, removed or added device variants, renamed signals, and changes to memory, boot, clock, and peripheral documentation.
sections.short_description: Records the initial releases and major early changes to the datasheet.

sections.title: Revision History: Revision 4 Updates
sections.summary: Continues the revision 4 change log with updates to USB OTG, power and reset behavior, current-consumption tables, PLL specifications, I/O and timer characteristics, ADC and DAC data, and interface timing. It also records changes to package documentation, thermal characteristics, application material, and selected figures.
sections.short_description: Details extensive revision 4 updates to features, electrical data, and peripherals.

sections.title: Revision History: Further Datasheet Changes
sections.summary: Continues the revision history with updates to I/O features, UART behavior, pin names and reserved pins, and support for the WLCSP64+2 package. Revisions also clarify power-supply supervisor and regulator behavior, VBAT operation, HSE limits, electrical ratings and operating conditions, reset thresholds, oscillator and PLL characteristics, USB support, and pin definitions.
sections.short_description: Highlights revisions to I/O, pins, electrical limits, power behavior, and package and USB support.

sections.title: Revision 6: Device features and pin mapping
sections.summary: Revision 6 introduces or clarifies SRAM1 and SRAM2, package availability, camera-interface support, and clock and regulator details. It also updates I2S sampling information, RTC and timer descriptions, USART baud-rate data, pin and alternate-function definitions, and power-supply diagrams and characteristics.
sections.short_description: Covers revision 6 updates to device features, clocks, peripherals, and pins.

sections.title: Revision 6: Power consumption and oscillator characteristics
sections.summary: This section lists updated run, sleep, stop, standby, and VBAT current-consumption data, including new figures and peripheral-current conditions. It also revises wake-up timings and external, LSE, HSI, and LSI oscillator parameters, with new temperature-related accuracy figures and notes.
sections.short_description: Details revisions to current-consumption, low-power, and oscillator data.

sections.title: Revision 6: PLL, memory, and interface characteristics
sections.summary: Revision 6 updates main PLL and audio PLL lock time, jitter, and current data, plus spread-spectrum and Flash-memory characteristics. It also revises EMI, ESD, I/O injection, timer, I2C, USB, Ethernet, ADC, DAC, and sensor specifications, and changes FSMC read/write timing diagrams and tables.
sections.short_description: Summarizes PLL, Flash, I/O, bus, and peripheral timing changes.

sections.title: Revision 6: FSMC and USB timing updates
sections.summary: The remaining revision 6 changes refine FSMC timing parameters and notes across synchronous memory, PC Card, and NAND controller tables and waveforms. The USB OTG HS host-only and peripheral-only connection figures are explicitly identified as operating in full-speed mode.
sections.short_description: Covers FSMC waveform changes and USB full-speed figure clarifications.

sections.title: Revisions 7 and 8
sections.summary: Revision 7 adds SDIO and revises voltage, PLL jitter, EMI, I2C, sensor, and ordering information, while updating package-level peripheral availability. Revision 8 updates memory maps and board compatibility, SRAM and USB documentation, pin alternate functions, peripheral mappings, and power-consumption and PLL spread-spectrum details.
sections.short_description: Summarizes added peripherals and subsequent memory, pin, and clock updates.

sections.title: Revision 8: December 2011 updates
sections.summary: Continuation of revision 8’s change log, covering updates to SPI, ULPI, Ethernet, FSMC, and DCMI characteristics and timing information. It also records a revised UFBGA package entry, changes to USB OTG interface solution diagrams and notes, the addition of Ethernet interface solutions, and an updated disclaimer.
sections.short_description: Summarizes revision 8 changes to interfaces, timing data, packages, and USB.

sections.title: Revisions 9 and 10: 2012 document updates
sections.summary: The 2012 entries describe revisions to supply limits, device features and package support, pin definitions, peripheral notes, and block diagrams. They also cover updates to operating and electrical characteristics, clocks, ADC and DAC data, memory timings, USB and Ethernet information, power-supply guidance, package drawings, and ordering or application references.
sections.short_description: Records 2012 changes to device features, operating data, interfaces, and packages.

sections.title: Revision 11: November 2013 updates
sections.summary: Revision 11 documents broad updates across the datasheet, including WLCSP64+2 usage, power and reset options, RTC features, operating conditions, pinout tables, alternate-function mappings, and electrical characteristics. It also notes changes to I2C, ADC, DAC, and memory timing information, removal of application block diagrams, and revisions to package outlines and mechanical data.
sections.short_description: Details revision 11 changes to pinouts, electrical characteristics, and package documentation.

sections.title: Revisions 12–18: 2014–2020 updates
sections.summary: The later change-log entries record updates to VBAT and general operating conditions, current-consumption notes, I/O susceptibility and reset characteristics, and package drawings and markings. Revisions 13–17 also update oscillator and PLL information, compatibility and package sections, asynchronous memory timings, and captions. Revision 18 updates USB OTG HS, reset and power-control data, I/O AC and PC Card/CF timings, and pin and oscillator footnotes.
sections.short_description: Summarizes later revisions to operating limits, package data, and peripheral specifications.

sections.title: Important Notice and Legal Disclaimer
sections.summary: STMicroelectronics reserves the right to change its products and documentation without notice and advises purchasers to obtain current information before ordering. Purchasers are responsible for product selection and use; no intellectual-property license is granted. The notice also addresses sales terms, warranty, trademarks, superseding information, and copyright.
sections.short_description: STMicroelectronics’ product, warranty, intellectual property, and trademark notice.
